item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00219","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C03","C21","C10"],"selected_candidate_label":"C03","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C03 is a direct and concrete drafting precursor. It sets out the same 1941 agreement, the same choice between joint United States-Canadian construction and a Canadian seaway if Congress fails to act, the same alternative application to the International Joint Commission, and the same appeal for prompt congressional action. The child updates that framework after the anticipated application was filed and expressly refers back to the April communication. C21 shares the project and several supporting arguments but lacks the child's distinctive alternative-procedure structure. C10 mentions the project and advocates immediate construction but is primarily an interagency resource-survey directive.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"These documents mark the official commencement of a procedure for getting the St. Lawrence project built if the Congress fails to approve the legislation which is before it for that purpose.","parent_excerpt":"Thus the arrangements are nearly completed for proceeding with the St. Lawrence project by an alternative means if the Congress fails to act soon on the 1941 Agreement.","explanation":"The child updates C03's anticipated alternative procedure from nearly completed arrangements to official commencement."},{"child_excerpt":"Under this procedure, the seaway will be built by the Canadian Government, and the power phase of the project will be built by the Province of Ontario and a United States entity authorized by the Congress or by the Federal Power Commission","parent_excerpt":"The Canadian Government is ready and willing to build a seaway ... on the Canadian side of the boundary, if the Congress does not authorize the United States Government to participate ... it will be necessary for the United States and Canada jointly to apply to the International Joint Commission","explanation":"Both describe substantially the same administrative machinery and division of responsibility triggered by congressional inaction."},{"child_excerpt":"I strongly recommend, therefore, that the Congress promptly complete action on legislation to carry out the 1941 agreement","parent_excerpt":"I strongly recommend that your committee and the Congress promptly complete action on this vital matter.","explanation":"The concluding operative appeal uses closely parallel language and serves the same function."}]}
